# 2 Chronicles Chapter 2 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** Solomon decided to build a temple for the name of the LORD and a royal palace for himself.

**2** He conscripted seventy thousand laborers, eighty thousand stonecutters in the hill country, and thirty-six hundred foremen to supervise them.

**3** Solomon sent this message to King Huram of Tyre: "Do for me what you did for my father David when you sent him cedar to build his palace.

**4** I am now building a temple for the name of the LORD my God, dedicating it to Him — for burning fragrant incense before Him, for the regular display of sacred bread, and for morning and evening burnt offerings on Sabbaths, New Moons, and the appointed festivals of the LORD our God. This is a permanent obligation for Israel.

**5** The temple I'm building will be magnificent, because our God is greater than all other gods.

**6** But who can really build a house for Him? The heavens — even the highest heavens — cannot contain Him! Who am I to build Him a temple, except as a place to burn incense before Him?

**7** So send me a master craftsman who can work with gold, silver, bronze, iron, and purple, crimson, and blue yarn — someone skilled in engraving — to work alongside the craftsmen here in Judah and Jerusalem whom my father David provided.

**8** Also send me cedar, cypress, and algum logs from Lebanon. I know your workers are experienced at cutting Lebanese timber. My workers will join yours

**9** to produce lumber in large quantities, because the temple I'm building will be impressively large.

**10** I will pay your woodcutters twenty thousand cors of ground wheat, twenty thousand cors of barley, twenty thousand baths of wine, and twenty thousand baths of olive oil."

**11** King Huram of Tyre sent Solomon a written reply: "Because the LORD loves His people, He has made you their king."

**12** Huram continued, "Praise the LORD, the God of Israel, who made heaven and earth! He has given King David a wise son with intelligence and discernment, who will build a temple for the LORD and a palace for himself.

**13** I am sending you Huram-abi, a master craftsman of great skill.

**14** His mother is from the tribe of Dan and his father is from Tyre. He is trained to work in gold, silver, bronze, iron, stone, and wood, as well as purple, blue, and crimson yarn and fine linen. He can execute any design and solve any problem put to him. He will work with your craftsmen and those of my lord David, your father.

**15** Now let my lord send the wheat, barley, olive oil, and wine he promised to his servants.

**16** We will cut all the timber you need from Lebanon and float it in rafts by sea to Joppa, and you can haul it up to Jerusalem."

**17** Solomon took a census of all the foreigners living in Israel — following the census his father David had conducted — and found there were 153,600.

**18** He assigned 70,000 as laborers, 80,000 as stonecutters in the hills, and 3,600 as foremen to keep the people working.


---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

- **2:6**: "Who can really build a house for Him?" — Solomon's theology is sophisticated: he knows a building can't contain God. The temple is a meeting point, not a cage. This prevents the idolatry of sacred architecture.

- **2:11**: A pagan king declaring that God made Solomon king because He loves Israel — this is one of the most remarkable theological statements in Chronicles, and it comes from an outsider.

- **2:17-18**: The Chronicler goes out of his way to note that the forced laborers were foreigners, not Israelites. Solomon does not enslave his own people — a key distinction from the Exodus narrative.


— PNEUMA
